# LaunchDarkly Documentation

> Learn how to ship features, AI updates, and releases with confidence using LaunchDarkly.

This is the LaunchDarkly documentation index for AI agents and LLMs, organized by product area. Each link below resolves to the markdown version of the page.

For the full documentation snapshot in one file, see [https://launchdarkly.com/docs/llms-full.txt](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/llms-full.txt).

## Get started

- [Welcome to LaunchDarkly Docs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home.md)
- [Launch Insights](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/launch-insights.md): This topic describes the Launch Insights dashboard. Launch Insights is an executive-level dashboard that summarizes how your organization is adopting the best practices associated with risk-free releases.
- [LaunchDarkly architecture](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/architecture.md): This topic gives a high-level explanation of LaunchDarkly's platform architecture.
- [LaunchDarkly vocabulary](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/vocabulary.md): This topic defines common words used in the LaunchDarkly application and documentation.

### Onboarding

- [Onboarding](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding.md): Quickstart guides to get up and running with LaunchDarkly SDKs in minutes.
- [Set up .NET (server-side) SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/dotnet-server.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly .NET (server-side) SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up Android SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/android.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly Android SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up Go SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/go.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly Go SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up iOS SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/ios.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly iOS SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up Java (server-side) SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/java.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly Java SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up JavaScript SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/javascript.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly JavaScript SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up Node.js (client-side) SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/node-client.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly Node.js (client-side) SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up Node.js (server-side) SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/node-server.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly Node.js (server-side) SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up Python SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/python.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly Python SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.
- [Set up React Native SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/react-native.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly React Native SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.

- [Set up Vue SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/onboarding/vue.md): Install and initialize the LaunchDarkly Vue SDK to start evaluating feature flags in your application.

### Get started

- [Get started with LaunchDarkly](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started.md): This topic walks you through creating a LaunchDarkly account, installing an SDK, and creating and targeting your first feature flag.
- [Exploring sample data](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/sample-data.md): This topic explains the sample flags, metrics, segments, and context kinds that LaunchDarkly creates for new trial accounts. It also explains how to use them to learn what LaunchDarkly can do.
- [Developer tools](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/dev-tools.md): LaunchDarkly offers several developer tools to help you work faster and more efficiently.
- [Vega](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/vega.md): This topic explains Vega, the LaunchDarkly AI-powered agent for investigating and fixing issues and managing feature flags.
- [Connecting Vega to GitHub](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/vega-github.md): This topic explains how to connect Vega to your GitHub account so that Vega can read code, make code changes, and open pull requests.
- [Using Vega in Slack](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/vega-slack.md): This topic explains how to use Vega directly in Slack to investigate issues, clean up flags, and interact with LaunchDarkly's AI agent from your team's workspace.
- [LaunchDarkly CLI](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/ldcli.md): This topic describes how to get started with the LaunchDarkly CLI.
- [LaunchDarkly CLI commands](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/ldcli-commands.md): This topic describes common commands and configuration options in the LaunchDarkly CLI.
- [LaunchDarkly MCP server](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/mcp.md): This topic explains how to get started with the LaunchDarkly Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
- [LaunchDarkly hosted MCP server](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/mcp-hosted.md): This topic explains how to connect your AI client to the LaunchDarkly hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
- [LaunchDarkly local MCP server](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/mcp-local.md): This topic describes how to get started with the LaunchDarkly local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
- [LaunchDarkly developer toolbar](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/dev-toolbar.md): This category has documentation topics about the LaunchDarkly developer toolbar.
- [Setting up the LaunchDarkly developer toolbar](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/dev-toolbar-setup.md): This topic describes how to install the LaunchDarkly developer toolbar.
- [Using the LaunchDarkly developer toolbar](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/dev-toolbar-using.md): This topic describes how to use the LaunchDarkly developer toolbar.
- [LaunchDarkly agent skills](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/skills.md): This topic describes the AI agent skills that LaunchDarkly offers for various AI applications.
- [IDE connectors and agents](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/ide.md): This category lists integrated development environment (IDE) connector integrations and agents for third-party apps.
- [IntelliJ IDEA](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/intellij.md): This topic explains how to use the LaunchDarkly IntelliJ IDEA plugin to interact with feature flags from within IntelliJ IDEs.
- [LaunchDarkly extension for GitHub Copilot](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/github-copilot-extension.md): This topic links to documentation on using the LaunchDarkly extension for GitHub Copilot on Visual Studio Marketplace.
- [Visual Studio Code (VSCode)](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/vscode.md): This topic explains how to use the LaunchDarkly VSCode extension to interact with feature flags from within VSCode.
- [Flag cleanup custom agent for GitHub Copilot](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/github-copilot-agent.md): This topic describes how to install and use the LaunchDarkly flag cleanup custom agent for GitHub Copilot.
- [Setting up an SDK](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/setting-up.md): This topic explains how to set up an SDK to begin using LaunchDarkly.
- [Joining an account](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/join-account.md): This topic explains how to join LaunchDarkly as a new account member.
- [Logging in with SSO](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/login-sso.md): This topic explains how to log into LaunchDarkly for the first time using an SSO provider.
- [Using feature management](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/feature-management.md): This topic discusses using feature management at a high level, describes some key parts of the LaunchDarkly user interface (UI), and suggests different ways to learn more about working in LaunchDarkly.
- [Getting started in different roles](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/getting-started/roles.md): This topic includes suggested paths through the LaunchDarkly documentation specific to your role.

## AgentControl

### AgentControl

- [AgentControl](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol.md): The topics in this category explain how to use LaunchDarkly AgentControl to manage your AgentControl configs. You can use AgentControl to customize, test, and roll out new large language models (LLMs) within your generative AI applications.
- [Quickstart for AgentControl](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/quickstart.md): This topic explains how to get started with LaunchDarkly AgentControl to manage, deploy, and update agent configurations without redeploying your application.

### Set up AgentControl configs

- [Create configs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/create.md): This topic explains how to create and update AgentControl.
- [Create and manage config variations](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/create-variation.md): This topic explains how to create and manage config variations.
- [Create and manage AI model configurations](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/create-model-config.md): This topic explains how to create and manage custom models to use in AgentControl.
- [Agent skills](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/agent-skills.md): This topic explains how to use agent skills to create, manage, and attach reusable agent instructions across AgentControl config variations.
- [Tools](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/tools.md): This topic explains how to manage and use tools in AgentControl.
- [Prompt snippets](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/snippets.md): This topic explains how to use prompt snippets to create, manage, and reuse prompts across AgentControl config variations.

### Config evaluations

- [Playgrounds](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/playground.md): This topic explains how to use LLM playgrounds to create and run evaluations that measure the quality of model outputs before deployment.
- [Offline evaluations](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/offline-evaluations.md): This topic explains how to use offline evaluations to validate config variations before releasing them to production.
- [Datasets](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/datasets.md): This topic explains how to create, manage, and use datasets for offline evaluations.
- [Online evaluations](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/online-evaluations.md): This topic describes how to run online evaluations on config variations by attaching judges that score responses for accuracy, relevance, and toxicity.
- [Judges](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/judges.md): This topic explains how to create and manage custom judges for online evaluations in AgentControl.
- [Run experiments with AgentControl](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/experimentation.md): This topic introduces the role of AgentControl configs in LaunchDarkly Experimentation.

### Agents

- [Agents](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/agents.md): This topic explains how to create and use agent-based configs to support structured, multi-step AI workflows with shared configuration, judge models that evaluate response quality, and performance monitoring.
- [Agent graphs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/agent-graphs.md): This topic explains how to create and use agent graphs to orchestrate multi-agent workflows with AgentControl.

### Deliver and monitor configs

- [Config targeting](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/target.md): This topic explains how to use AgentControl config targeting to control which of your customers receive a particular variation of a config, based on their context.
- [Monitor config performance](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/monitor.md): This topic explains how to monitor the performance of your configs.
- [Understand AI impact with AI Insights](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/insights.md): This topic explains how to use AI insights to understand the impact of AgentControl configs by analyzing metrics across your project.
- [The trends explorer](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/trends.md): This topic explains how to use the AgentControl trends explorer to view aggregated performance data across multiple configs, providers, and models.
- [Manually instrument LLM spans](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/manual-llm-span-tracing.md): This topic explains how to manually instrument LLM spans so LaunchDarkly can observe model activity when automatic instrumentation is not available.

### Agent optimization

- [Agent optimization](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/optimization.md): This topic explains what agent optimization is, its different modes, and how to start using it.
- [Optimization SDK quickstart](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/optimization-quickstart.md): This topic explains how to configure the SDK to use agent optimization.
- [Performing optimization runs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/optimization-runs.md): This topic explains how to run an optimization by pulling its configuration from LaunchDarkly.
- [Optimization runs without a config](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/optimize-without-config.md): This topic explains how to define judges, model choices, and evaluation parameters directly in code without a LaunchDarkly configuration object.
- [Expected output mode](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/ground-truth-optimization.md): This topic explains how to use Expected output mode to optimize an agent against known input/output pairs.
- [Using tools in agent optimization](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/optimization-tools.md): This topic explains how to pass tool definitions through to your agent and judge calls during optimization runs.
- [Other framework examples for agent optimization](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/optimization-framework-examples.md): Code examples for the Optimization SDK using OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain, Strands, and the Claude Agent SDK.
- [OptimizationContext reference](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/optimization-context.md): This topic has a full field reference for the OptimizationContext object returned by all optimization methods.

### Manage AgentControl

- [Manage AgentControl](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/manage.md): This topic explains how to view and manage AgentControl.
- [Adaptive triggers](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/triggers.md): This topic explains how to use adaptive triggers in configs to mitigate the effect of unexpected outages or performance degradation in your LLM provider.
- [AgentControl and information privacy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/privacy.md): This topic describes how the LaunchDarkly AgentControl product treats personally identifiable information (PII).
- [Compare config variation versions](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/compare-variation-versions.md): This topic explains how to compare versions of a config variation.
- [Configure Amazon Bedrock](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/configure-amazon-bedrock.md): This topic explains how to configure Amazon Bedrock as a model provider.
- [Configure token limits](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/agentcontrol/configure-token-limits.md): This topic explains how to configure token limits for offline evaluations in AgentControl.

## Feature flags

### Create flags

- [Create flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/create.md): This category explains how to use LaunchDarkly to create your feature flags.
- [Creating new flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/new.md): This topic explains how to create new feature flags in LaunchDarkly.
- [Flag types](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/types.md): This topic explains the four types of feature flags and when to use them.
- [Turning flags on and off](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/toggle.md): This topic explains how to enable and disable flags from the Flags list.
- [Creating flag variations](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/variations.md): This topic explains how to create and edit your feature flag's variations and outlines the different types of flag variations.
- [Cloning existing flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/clone.md): This topic explains how to create new flags by cloning existing flags in LaunchDarkly.
- [Importing flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/import.md): This topic explains how to import flags from other feature management tools into LaunchDarkly.
- [Flag settings](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/flag-settings.md): This topic explains how to edit a feature flag's environment-specific and project-wide settings.

### Target with flags

- [Target with flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/target.md): This topic explains how to use flag targeting to control which of your customers receive a variation of a feature flag, based on their context.
- [Targeting rules](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/target-rules.md): This topic explains how to use flag targeting rules to serve flag variations to different contexts based on their attributes.
- [Manage targeting rules](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/manage-rules.md): This topic explains how to manage flag targeting rules.
- [Individual targeting](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/individual-targeting.md): This topic explains how to control which individual contexts receive a variation of a feature flag, based on the context key.
- [Bulk targeting](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/bulk-targeting.md): This topic explains how to perform edits on groups of contexts, or export all the contexts a flag is targeted to.
- [Mobile targeting](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/mobile-targeting.md): This topic explains how to control which mobile apps and devices receive a variation of a feature flag.
- [Custom rules](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/custom-rules.md): This topic explains how to use custom rules to target contexts based on their attributes.
- [JSON targeting](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/json-targeting.md): This topic explains how to create and edit flag targeting rules using JSON.
- [Converting rules into segments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/rules-segments.md): This topic explains how convert targeting rules into reusable segments.
- [Testing changes to flag targeting](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/preview-rules.md): This topic explains how to use the test run feature to find out which variation a particular context will receive for a given feature flag.
- [Adaptive triggers](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/triggers.md): This topic explains how to use adaptive triggers to automatically serve a different flag variation and send an alert when a metric indicates a problem.

### Flag templates

- [Flag templates](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/templates.md): This topic explains the different types of flags available in LaunchDarkly.
- [Custom flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/custom.md): This topic explains how to get started with custom flags.
- [Release flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/release.md): This topic explains how you can use release flags to progressively roll out functionality.
- [Kill switch flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/killswitch.md): This topic explains how you can use kill switch or circuit breaker flags to shut off functionality.
- [Experiment flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/experiment.md): This topic explains how you can use experiment flags to test a hypothesis.
- [Migration flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/migration.md): This topic explains how you can use migration flags to take the complexity and risk out of modernizing your tech stack.
- [Creating migration flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/create-migration.md): This topic explains how you can create migration flags.
- [Targeting with migration flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/target-migration.md): This topic explains how you can target contexts using migration flags.
- [Migration flag metrics](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/migration-metrics.md): This topic explains how you can use metrics to track the progress of a migration flag.

### Manage flags

- [Manage flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/manage.md): This category explains how to organize your flags across different environments in your LaunchDarkly project.
- [The Flags list](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/list.md): This topic explains how to use the Flags list, which shows your feature flags and gives you options to create, modify, and manage them.
- [Flag links](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/links.md): This topic explains how to create and use flag links to view external mentions of flags and relevant materials from other tools and services.
- [Following flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/follow.md): This topic explains how to follow flags. Following a flag sends you email and Slack notifications when someone makes a targeting change to that flag.
- [Comparing and copying flag settings](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/compare-copy.md): This topic explains how to compare and copy flag settings between two environments.
- [Viewing flags across environments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/view-across.md): This topic explains how to view flags across multiple environments.
- [Deprecating flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/deprecate.md): This topic explains how to deprecate flags you no longer need.
- [Archiving and restoring flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/archive.md): This topic explains how to archive flags you no longer need and how to restore archived flags.
- [Deleting flags](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/delete.md): This topic explains how to permanently delete flags that are already archived.
- [Flag prerequisites](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/prereqs.md): This topic explains how to use feature flag prerequisites to enable or disable features based on different states.
- [The off variation](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/off-variation.md): This topic explains how to set the off variation for a flag.
- [The default rule](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/default-rule.md): This topic explains how to set the default rule for a flag.
- [Flag statuses and lifecycle stages](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/flag-status.md): This topic explains what the different flag statuses are, and how they relate to a flag's lifecycle.
- [Flag lifecycle settings](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/flag-lifecycle-settings.md): This topic describes flag lifecycle settings and how to update them. The flag lifecycle settings let you customize the criteria that LaunchDarkly uses to determine when flags are ready to be archived.
- [Project-level flag settings](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/proj-flag-settings.md): This topic describes project-level flag settings and how to update them.
- [Vega for flag cleanup](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/manage/flag-cleanup-vega.md): This topic explains how to use Vega to identify and remove stale feature flags from your codebase, including automated scheduled cleanup.

### Code references

- [Code references](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/code-references.md): This topic explains how to use code references in LaunchDarkly to find and manage references to your feature flags. Code references help you determine which projects reference your feature flags and remove technical debt.
- [Bitbucket code references](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/code-references/bitbucket.md): This topic explains how to use the ld-find-code-refs utility with Bitbucket code references to create code references in LaunchDarkly.
- [CircleCI code references](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/code-references/circleci.md): This topic explains how you can use the ld-find-code-refs utility with CircleCI to automatically populate code references in LaunchDarkly.
- [Custom configuration with ld-find-code-refs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/code-references/custom-config.md): This topic gives a high-level explanation of how to use the ld-find-code-refs script to perform other functions.
- [GitHub code references](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/code-references/github-actions.md): This topic explains how to use the ld-find-code-refs utility with GitHub code references to automatically populate code references in LaunchDarkly.
- [GitLab code references](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/code-references/gitlab.md): This topic explains how to set up and configure the GitLab code references to use with LaunchDarkly. You can use the ld-find-code-refs utility with GitLab code references to automatically populate code references in LaunchDarkly.

### Contexts

- [Contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/contexts.md): This category has documentation topics about LaunchDarkly contexts. Contexts are people, services, machines, or other resources that encounter feature flags in your product.
- [An introduction to contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/contexts/intro.md): This topic summarizes what contexts are and provides resources to learn how to use them.
- [The Contexts list](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/contexts-list.md): This topic explains what the Contexts list is, how it is populated, and how to use it.
- [Filtering the Contexts list](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/contexts-list-filtering.md): This topic explains how to filter contexts on the Contexts list. You can filter contexts on the Contexts list by context kind, name, key, or attribute.
- [The context details page](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/context-details.md): This topic explains what the context details page is. The context details page gives you a detailed view of a context and lets you customize its experience from one screen.
- [Context instances](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/context-instances.md): This topic includes information about context instances.
- [Context kinds](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/context-kinds.md): This topic explains what context kinds are and how to use them.
- [Viewing context kinds](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/context-kinds-view.md): This topic explains how to view context kinds.
- [Creating and editing context kinds](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/context-kinds-create.md): This topic explains how to create and edit context kinds.
- [Archiving context kinds](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/context-kinds-archive.md): This topic explains how to archive and restore archived context kinds.
- [Context attributes](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/context-attributes.md): This topic explains what context attributes are, how to configure them, and how LaunchDarkly uses them to evaluate flags and display flag variations to your customers.
- [Built-in attributes](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/built-in-attributes.md): This topic explains what built-in attributes are and how to configure them.
- [Custom attributes](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/custom-attributes.md): This topic explains what custom context attributes are and how to configure them.
- [Using private context attributes](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/private-context-attributes.md): This topic explains how to create targeting rules that target contexts based on attributes that may or may not be stored in LaunchDarkly.
- [Multi-contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/multi-contexts.md): This topic includes information about multi-contexts and context instances. Contexts are people, services, machines, or other resources that encounter feature flags in your product.
- [Anonymous contexts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/anonymous-contexts.md): This topic explains what anonymous contexts are, how their information is handled in LaunchDarkly, and how they contribute to your monthly account usage.

### Segments

- [Segments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/segments.md): This topic introduces the concept of segments. Segments let you target groups of contexts individually or by attribute.
- [Creating segments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/segments-create.md): This topic explains how to create rule-based, smaller list-based, larger list-based, and synced segments.
- [Targeting contexts in rule-based and smaller list-based segments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/rule-based-segments.md): This topic explains how to target contexts in rule-based and smaller list-based segments.
- [Targeting contexts in larger list-based segments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/list-based-segments.md): This topic explains how to target contexts within larger list-based segments.
- [Targeting segments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/segment-targeting.md): This topic explains how to target a segment in a flag rule.
- [Managing segments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/segment-management.md): This topic explains how to edit and delete segments.
- [Segment types](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/segment-types.md): This topic explains different segment types and when to use them.
- [Segments synced from external tools](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/synced-segments.md): This topic explains how to create segments that sync with an external tool.
- [Syncing segments with Amplitude cohorts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/amplitude.md): This topic explains how to create segments that sync with an Amplitude cohort.
- [Syncing segments with Fivetran (formerly Census)](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/fivetran.md): This topic links to Fivetran's documentation for its LaunchDarkly synced segment integration.
- [Syncing segments with Heap](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/heap.md): This topic links to Heap's documentation for its LaunchDarkly synced segment integration.
- [Syncing segments with Hightouch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/hightouch.md): This topic links to Hightouch's documentation for its LaunchDarkly synced segment integration.
- [Syncing segments with RudderStack Audiences](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/rudderstack.md): This topic links to RudderStack's documentation for its LaunchDarkly synced segment integration.
- [Syncing segments with Tealium Audiences](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/flags/tealium.md): This topic links to Tealium's documentation for its LaunchDarkly synced segment integration.

### Cheatsheets

- [Cheatsheets](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/cheatsheets.md): This section contains high-level summaries of how to achieve certain outcomes with AgentControl configs and other LaunchDarkly features, such as Experimentation and guarded rollouts.

It covers rolling back code, swapping AI models, and rerouting traffic without a human in the loop.
- [Optimize AI performance and cost with AgentControl configs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/cheatsheets/optimize-ai-cost.md): This guide shows how to use LaunchDarkly AgentControl configs to define prompt and model variations, evaluate them against real production traffic, and route to the best-performing option.
- [Run continuous experiments in production](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/cheatsheets/continuous-experiments.md): This guide shows how to use LaunchDarkly to run continuous experiments across both code and AgentControl configs. You define variations, measure their impact against production traffic, and promote winners without redeploying.
- [Ship AI-built code with AgentControl or CodeControl](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/cheatsheets/ai-code.md): This guide shows how to use LaunchDarkly to release AI-built changes safely. Gradual rollouts, defined guardrails, automated detection, and instant remediation if something goes wrong, with no redeploys.

- [Building a chatbot with multiple AI providers using AgentControl configs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/agentcontrol/best-practices.md): This guide teaches you how to build a simple AI-powered chatbot using LaunchDarkly AgentControl with multiple AI providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.

### Observability

- [Observability](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/observability.md): This category has guides that teach you how to use Observability.
- [Getting started with observability for .NET MAUI](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/observability/getting-started-maui.md): This guide shows how to add LaunchDarkly observability and session replay to a .NET MAUI application targeting Android and iOS, and confirm telemetry is flowing.
- [Getting started with observability for Android](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/observability/getting-started-android.md): This guide shows how to add LaunchDarkly observability and session replay to an Android application using Kotlin or Java, and confirm telemetry is flowing.
- [When to use session replay, traces, logs, and Vega](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/observability/when-to-use-session-replay-traces-logs.md): Session replay, traces, and logs each answer a different question about your application, and Vega is the agent that investigates them for you. This topic explains when to use each.

### Experimentation

- [Experimentation](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation.md): This category has guides that teach you how to use Experimentation.
- [Building your first experiment](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/building.md): This guide explains how to create your first experiment in LaunchDarkly. By the end, you'll have a running experiment with a flag, an audience, and one or more metrics.
- [Creating an A/B experiment using a funnel metric group](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/funnel-optimization.md): This guide provides an example of how to create and read the results of a an A/B experiment using a funnel metric group.
- [Creating mutually exclusive experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/mutually-exclusive.md): This guide provides an example of how to create mutually exclusive experiments using experiment layers.
- [Designing experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/designing-experiments.md): This guide provides strategies and best practices to design an effective experiment in LaunchDarkly.
- [Example experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/example-experiments.md): This guide provides examples of experiments you can build in LaunchDarkly.
- [Experimentation best practices](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/best-practices.md): This topic includes some recommended best practices for using LaunchDarkly Experimentation.
- [Bayesian versus frequentist statistics](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/bayesian-frequentist.md): This guide explains the difference between Bayesian and frequentist statistics, both of which are available in LaunchDarkly’s Experimentation framework.
- [Maintaining consistency across user sessions when running experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/logged-out-logged-in.md): This guide provides strategies to manage experiments that include users with multiple user sessions interacting with your app.
- [Measuring Experimentation impact with holdouts](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/holdouts.md): This guide explains how to create a holdout group to measure the effectiveness of your Experimentation program.
- [Migrating from Statsig to LaunchDarkly Experimentation](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/migrate-from-statsig.md): This guide explains how to migrate your Statsig experiment implementation to LaunchDarkly Experimentation.
- [Proving ROI with data-driven AI agent experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/ai-experiments-roi.md): This guide explains how to measure and prove the return on investment (ROI) of AI model changes with LaunchDarkly experiments.
- [Sample size calculations for frequentist experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/experimentation/sample-size-calc.md): This guide explains why sample size calculations are important for frequentist experiments, and how to calculate them.

### Statistical methodology

- [Statistical methodology](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology.md): This category has guides that explain the statistical methodology LaunchDarkly uses in its Experimentation product.
- [Choosing a statistical methodology](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology/choosing.md): This guide explains how to choose a statistical methodology for your LaunchDarkly experiments.
- [Covariate adjustment and CUPED methodology](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology/cuped.md): This guide explains the methodology and usage of CUPED (Controlled experiments Using Pre-Experiment Data) for covariate adjustment in LaunchDarkly Experimentation results.
- [Statistical methodology for Bayesian experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology/methodology-bayesian.md): This guide explains the statistical methodology LaunchDarkly uses to calculate Bayesian experiment variation means, and how these analytics formulas are useful for validating your results.
- [Statistical methodology for frequentist experiments](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology/methodology-frequentist.md): This guide explains the statistical methodology LaunchDarkly uses to calculate frequentist experiment variation means, and how these analytics formulas are useful for validating your results.
- [Multiple comparisons correction](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology/mcc.md): This guide explains the methodology LaunchDarkly uses to perform multiple comparisons corrections on frequentist experiment results.
- [Stratified sampling](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology/stratified-sampling.md): This topic explains how to use stratified sampling to re-randomize the contexts in your experiment treatments. Re-randomization helps eliminate covariate imbalance and reduce false positives and false negatives in your experiment results.
- [Sample ratio mismatch](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/statistical-methodology/sample-ratios.md): This guide explains what sample ratios are and how to detect a sample ratio mismatch (SRM).

It helps you determine which type of SDK to use.

- [Domain list](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/concepts/domain-list.md): This topic explains which domains the LaunchDarkly SDKs connect to by default.
- [Evaluation reasons](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/concepts/evaluation-reasons.md): This topic explains how to use LaunchDarkly to determine why a context instance receives a given flag variation.
- [Flag evaluation rules in server-side SDKs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/concepts/flag-evaluation-rules.md): This topic explains the algorithm used to evaluate a feature flag. This document is intended to be used by developers contributing to or building server-side SDKs for LaunchDarkly.
- [Persistent data stores](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/concepts/data-stores.md): This topic explains what a persistent feature store is and how a persistent feature store can keep flag data.
- [Sample applications](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/concepts/sample-applications.md): This topic lists the sample applications available for learning how to work with LaunchDarkly SDKs.

- [Version notifications](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/concepts/version-notifications.md): This topic explains how to set up notifications to learn about version updates and end of life notices for LaunchDarkly's SDKs.
- [Versioning policy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/concepts/versioning.md): This topic explains LaunchDarkly's SDK versioning policy, which is based on the semantic versioning standard.

### Relay Proxy

- [The Relay Proxy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy.md): This topic explains what the Relay Proxy is and how to use it. The Relay Proxy is a small Go application that connects to the LaunchDarkly streaming API and proxies that connection to clients within your organization's network.
- [Determining whether to use the Relay Proxy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/determining.md): This category contains topics about how to decide whether to use the Relay Proxy.
- [Relay Proxy use cases](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/use-cases.md): This topic explains common Relay Proxy use cases and how to decide whether to use the Relay Proxy with your configuration.
- [Relay Proxy guidelines](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/guidelines.md): This topic includes guidelines for configuring and using the Relay Proxy successfully.
- [Relay Proxy Enterprise](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/enterprise.md): This section explains the features that are available for Enterprise customers who use the Relay Proxy.
- [Automatic configuration](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/automatic-configuration.md): This topic explains how to set up the Relay Proxy's automatic configuration feature. This feature is for customers on Enterprise plans.
- [Offline mode](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/offline.md): This topic explains how to configure the Relay Proxy to run without a network connection. This feature is for customers on Enterprise plans.
- [Implementing the Relay Proxy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/implementing.md): This topic explains how to implement the Relay Proxy.
- [Configuring and deploying the Relay Proxy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/deploying.md): This topic explains how to configure and deploy the Relay Proxy.
- [Relay Proxy deployment strategies](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/deployment-strategies.md): This topic describes two recommended deployment strategies for the Relay Proxy based on common use cases.
- [Configuring SDKs for the Relay Proxy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/sdk-config.md): This topic explains how to set up and use the Relay Proxy. It explains the Relay Proxy's two modes and how to perform flag evaluations with the Relay Proxy.
- [Monitoring the Relay Proxy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/monitoring.md): This topic explains best practices for monitoring the Relay Proxy as it runs, as well as information about exporting metrics and other data.
- [Upgrading the Relay Proxy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/upgrading.md): This topic explains how to upgrade, roll back, and validate deployments of the Relay Proxy, and what to do when a version approaches its end-of-life date.
- [Versioning policy](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/relay-proxy/versioning.md): This topic explains LaunchDarkly's Relay Proxy versioning policy, which is based on the semantic versioning standard.

- [Using LaunchDarkly feature flags and Experimentation with Wordpress](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/wordpress.md): This tutorial teaches you how to install and configure a LaunchDarkly SDK in a self-hosted WordPress environment, use feature flags for controlled rollouts and targeted content, and set up A/B experiments across a WordPress landing page.

### AgentControl configs

- [Use LaunchDarkly AgentControl to control model administration with LiteLLM](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/agentcontrol-litellm-gateway.md): Centralized model routing, prompt governance, and telemetry for any OpenAI-compatible application, with no code changes.

- [Optimize an AI agent to sound human, with a judge you own](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/agent-optimization.md): Use LaunchDarkly agent optimization to make an AI agent's replies sound human. Agent optimization rewrites the prompt against GPTZero, an AI detector wired in as an inverted judge, then you run a fuller eval on the candidates it surfaces.
- [Benchmark LangGraph, Strands, OpenAI Agents, and Google ADK on the same agent graph](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/agent-graph-experiments.md): Benchmark LangGraph, Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Google ADK by running all four over one LaunchDarkly agent graph with the model held constant. An experiment ranks them on latency and tokens with an LLM-as-a-judge quality guardrail, then the same flag promotes the winner to production with no redeploy.
- [Migrate a hardcoded LangGraph agent to LaunchDarkly AgentControl in 20 minutes](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/ld4a-langgraph-migration.md): Migrate from the official langchain-ai/react-agent template from hardcoded prompts, models, and tools to a full AgentControl implementation using the migrate agent skill.

- [Beyond n8n for workflow automation: agent graphs as your universal agent harness](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/agent-graphs.md): Build multi-agent systems that work across LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, and other frameworks. One graph definition, real-time monitoring, config changes without deploys.

Build a three-agent pipeline and wire it to LangGraph.
- [Compare AI orchestrators: LangGraph vs Strands vs OpenAI Swarm](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/ai-orchestrators.md): Build the same AI swarm across LangGraph, Strands, and OpenAI Swarm. Compare real performance data and learn framework-agnostic agent configuration.
- [The AI iteration loop for deploying reliable agents with LangGraph](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/tutorials/ai-iteration-loop-for-reliable-agents.md): Set the foundation for an AI iteration loop with LaunchDarkly feature flags, AgentControl, and variation targeting, using a LangGraph decor agent as a running example.
